goals_presented_to_final_audit.description: Retain the verified parsed container for immutable accepted bytes in an implementation-owned handle. Give the handle a limited lifetime.
Extract shared metadata construction from the ordinary reader. Make both reader paths use it. Preserve every metadata, profile, rate, slack, plane-range, geometry, scale-shape and shard check.
Add accepted-wire decoding that uses the retained container without another container parse. Run the full plane materialization and reconstruction checks.
Add a deterministic CPU test with a tiny valid wire. Count calls to the real container parser across verification and accepted-wire decoding. Assert exactly one call.
Add a CPU comparison test for the accepted and ordinary reader paths. Require equal metadata and equal decoded values.

Add real-verifier and real-reader refusal tests for corrupt bytes, receipt size and hash mismatches, receipt-field mismatches, expected-identity mismatches, incomplete planes, wrong recipes and malformed metadata. Preserve existing refusals.
Refuse handles that verification did not issue. Cover a handle for other bytes.
Make the new fixtures self-contained and deterministic. Require no GPU, checkpoint or model download. Do not use artifact-dependent or device-dependent skips as proof for the new cases.
Add no global digest cache or extra copy of the large plane data. Keep retained evidence within the handle's lifetime.

Preserve existing function signatures and bytes-taking behavior. Keep serialized bytes, receipt fields, recipes, historical-producer verification, serving admission and source identities unchanged. Leave the existing plane-region digest fix unchanged.

Keep manual edits inside the four declared source and test files. Keep the four control test files read-only. Touch no protected path. Complete the relevant architecture and generator dependency reads. Use configured generation for declared outputs before checks. Never hand-edit generated outputs. Keep PrismaQuant adoption outside this change.

Run development and targeted pytest through PrismaBuild. Cover both edited test files and all four named read-only controls. Use native_threads_2. Retain the required execution records. Keep priority -10, admitted CPU and memory, and bounded workers as source requirements. Report unsupported controls and artifacts as evidence gaps. Do not claim that receipts prove them.

Establish independent assertion RED and GREEN proof for the new parse-count observer. Run head observers against base subjects for RED. Run the same observers against head subjects for GREEN. Require the base run to reach a failing parser-count assertion. Declare its exact RED message before execution. Do not accept an import or setup failure as that proof.

proof_obligation.quote: The parse-count check does not satisfy the declared RED proof. The base run fails before it reaches a parser-count assertion. Supply a proof that meets the subject/observer rule.

goals_presented_to_final_audit.description: Run the targeted tests independently again on the final head through PrismaBuild. Cover tests/test_cached_producer.py and tests/test_cached_unit_reader_gamut.py. Include tests/test_parse_digest_once.py, tests/test_compact_loader.py, tests/test_issue_refs.py and tests/test_impacted_tests.py as read-only controls. Use native_threads_2. Confirm that the new tests pass without a GPU, checkpoint or download. Retain the required records. Report unsupported evidence details as gaps.
Review the final diff for the declared edit boundary and protected-path restrictions. Confirm that the change preserves the stated APIs, validation rules and memory limits.
Publish the producer capability before PrismaQuant adopts it.
